editorial:
Imagine watching a slow-burn Italian drama and then suddenly getting hit with disaster movie footage. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a group of people dealing with their own personal problems and messy relationships, but the vibe changes completely when the producers threw in footage of a real earthquake to make it more exciting. It feels like two different movies fighting for space, which gives it a weird, dreamlike quality that you do not see often. It is less about the disaster and more about how people act when everything falls apart around them.

The acting is decent for the time, though the pacing can feel a bit slow until the chaos kicks in. You will probably notice that the earthquake scenes look a bit out of place, but that actually makes it a fun curiosity for movie buffs. If you love weird cinema history, you should definitely try to find this. Since it is a rare find, you might want to look for a digital rental on Apple TV or try and snag a physical copy for your collection to keep the quality high. It is a strange ride, but one that stays with you.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the aftermath of the disaster. After all the shaking stops and the dust settles, the characters are left to pick up the pieces of their lives. The final scenes focus on who survived and how their relationships changed because of the tragedy. It ends on a bittersweet note, showing that while the buildings are gone, the emotional scars remain, leaving you to wonder if they will ever truly recover.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange old Italian films and disaster stories.
